claims.text: Adding 2–5 wt% silicon to ZrB2 will enable processing at approximately 1700 °C by assisting densification.
During service, silicon-doped ZrB2 will form a protective SiO2-rich surface layer.
The SiO2-rich layer will enhance oxidation resistance relative to single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The SiO2-rich layer will enhance resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing above 2300 °C.
Lower-temperature undoped ZrB2 has compromised densification and phase integrity.
Conventional and lower-temperature ZrB2 are vulnerable to oxidation and liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Silicon induces lattice distortions in ZrB2 that enhance densification at lower temperatures.
Silicon concentrates at ZrB2 grain boundaries and surfaces.
Grain-boundary and surface silicon forms a continuous or semi-continuous amorphous silica layer during service.
Silicon facilitates liquid-phase sintering of ZrB2 at approximately 1700 °C.
Residual silicon preferentially oxidizes to form a protective SiO2-based scale.
The SiO2-based scale inhibits further oxidation and minimizes chemical attack by liquid plating metals.
Si-doped ZrB2 processed at approximately 1700 °C will have strength and structural integrity similar to or better than high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Si-doped ZrB2 will show significantly improved oxidation durability and liquid-metal corrosion resistance relative to both comparison groups.
The intervention is effective only near 2–5 wt% Si and a processing temperature of approximately 1700 °C.
Substantial deviations from the proposed silicon range or processing temperature may cause unwanted phase separation or prevent formation of an effective silica layer.
At sufficiently high service temperatures, the protective silica layer may destabilize.
